action: Pinned-source call-order audit of rust-sdk modern discover startup versus direct-peer setup and request-metadata requirement.
result: At the pinned commit, the client discover path creates a Peer, enters ClientLifecycleMode::Discover, and calls discover_startup. In discover_startup's successful modern branch, after version selection it sets peer_info, then immediately calls peer.set_client_request_metadata with the selected protocol version plus local client_info and client_capabilities, and only then returns DiscoverOutcome::Modern. The caller exits the lifecycle match and only afterward enters serve_inner. Therefore client_request_metadata is populated before the first ordinary post-discover Peer send handled by serve_inner. RoleClient::configure_direct_peer is not part of this discover path; it belongs to the separate direct-peer helper, where Peer construction is followed by R::configure_direct_peer before serve_inner. The pinned server source separately calls peer.require_request_metadata after constructing a server-side Peer in its modern request-serving path; that AtomicBool is a receive-side requirement and is not an attachment gate in the client discover sequence. Thus the previous unresolved child is resolved for client call ordering: set_client_request_metadata precedes DiscoverOutcome::Modern return, which precedes ordinary serve_inner sends.
